Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A battery bushing for a rechargeable battery has a mounting section and a contacting section. There is a torque ring, between the mounting section and the contacting section. The torque ring or the outer surface itself can be endowed with several indentations. The mounting section is configured to hold the battery bushing within a battery cover, into which it preferably is injection molded. The battery bushing is a hollow body, which has an outer wall and an inner wall. At the contacting section, the outer wall is conically shaped. At the mounting section, the outer wall has at least one circumferential projection forming a labyrinth. The inner wall comprises at least two sections. An upper section is approximately surrounded by the contacting section, and preferably has a conical shape. A lower section is approximately surrounded by the mounting section. The lower section preferably has (in a lateral sectional view) a concave shape. Between the upper section and the lower section, there may be an edge or a step.

outputs.L4:
A rechargeable-battery bushing is configured to be embedded in a battery cover and to provide a mechanically secure, electrically conductive, and fluid-tight connection between an internal battery terminal and an external connector. The bushing is formed as a hollow, generally rotationally symmetrical body having a mounting section and a contacting section. These sections are separated by a circumferential torque-transmitting ring, which may include one or more indentations, recesses, or other noncircular features. During manufacture, the bushing is positioned in a mold and incorporated into the battery cover by injection molding.

The mounting section is shaped to anchor the bushing firmly in the surrounding cover material. Its outer contour may include tapered or conical surfaces that allow the molded material to surround and retain the bushing in both axial directions. The torque ring provides additional resistance to rotation by creating a positive mechanical interlock with the cover. When the ring is indented or otherwise profiled, forces applied while tightening or loosening an external terminal connection are transferred into the battery cover without allowing the bushing to turn.

A circumferential projection is provided on the outer surface of the bushing. When the battery-cover material is molded around this projection, the projection cooperates with adjacent surfaces to form a labyrinth-like sealing path. This extended and interrupted interface reduces the likelihood that electrolyte, moisture, or gas will pass between the metal bushing and the surrounding plastic. The projection also contributes to axial retention and helps prevent the bushing from being pulled out of the cover.

The contacting section includes conical contact surfaces adapted to engage a corresponding terminal component. The tapered geometry promotes self-centering and produces a large, reliable contact area when the components are pressed or fitted together. This improves electrical conductivity while also increasing mechanical stability. The hollow interior permits connection to the internal current-carrying element of the rechargeable battery and may receive a terminal post, connector, or fastening element.

At its lower end, the interior of the bushing has a concave contour. This shape facilitates secure attachment to the internal terminal structure, provides space for material displacement or joining operations, and helps distribute mechanical and electrical loads. It can also improve manufacturability by avoiding abrupt transitions and by supporting consistent filling and flow during molding.

Together, the shaped mounting section, profiled torque ring, conical contacting surfaces, circumferential sealing projection, and concave lower interior provide a bushing that can be molded reliably into a battery cover. The resulting assembly offers strong resistance to axial withdrawal and rotation, effective sealing against leakage, efficient torque transfer, and a durable low-resistance electrical connection.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the structure and key features of a battery bushing for a rechargeable battery based on a patent specification.
counterfactuals.output:
A battery bushing for a rechargeable battery—particularly a lead-acid battery—is generally a conductive, sleeve-like terminal component mounted through the battery cover. Its principal features are:

- **Tubular body:** Defines an axial opening that receives or connects to an internal pole or terminal post.
- **External terminal portion:** Projects above the battery cover and provides the electrical connection to a cable, clamp, or threaded connector.
- **Internal connection portion:** Extends into the battery and is welded, fused, or otherwise electrically joined to the plate-group pole strap.
- **Mounting flange or shoulder:** Positions the bushing in the cover and limits axial movement.
- **Circumferential ribs, grooves, or undercuts:** Become embedded in the molded cover material, creating a long leakage path and improving resistance to electrolyte migration.
- **Anti-rotation formations:** Flats, teeth, knurling, or noncircular sections mechanically lock the bushing into the cover so that terminal torque is not transmitted to the internal connection.
- **Sealing region:** Cooperates with the cover material and, in some embodiments, a gasket or sealing compound to provide a liquid- and gas-tight joint.
- **Corrosion-resistant conductive construction:** Commonly formed from lead or a lead alloy in lead-acid batteries, with selected regions optionally plated, reinforced, or made as a composite insert.

The design therefore combines three functions: conducting current between the internal electrodes and the external terminal, mechanically anchoring the terminal in the battery cover, and preventing electrolyte or gas leakage along the terminal-cover interface.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise technical summary of an injection-molded battery terminal bushing, including its mounting section, contacting section, torque ring, and inner and outer wall geometries.
counterfactuals.output: An injection-molded battery terminal bushing is a conductive insert embedded in a molded battery cover. It includes a mounting section encapsulated by the cover material and a contacting section projecting outward for electrical connection. A circumferential torque ring on the mounting section mechanically locks the bushing against rotation and axial displacement. The inner wall defines a terminal-receiving bore, which may be cylindrical, tapered, stepped, or threaded to provide controlled electrical and mechanical engagement. The outer wall incorporates noncircular, tapered, ribbed, grooved, or undercut surfaces that promote resin flow, improve sealing, and increase resistance to torque and pullout.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain the design of a hollow battery bushing that is secured in a battery cover and uses circumferential projections to form a labyrinth seal.
counterfactuals.output:
A hollow battery bushing is typically a conductive, tube-shaped terminal insert molded or otherwise fixed into an opening in a molded battery cover.

- **Hollow body:** The bushing has an axial bore that receives a battery post, terminal stem, or connector. Its outer surface is surrounded by the cover material.
- **Circumferential projections:** Several axially spaced annular ribs or flanges extend around the bushing’s exterior. They may differ in diameter or have tapered faces to improve molding and retention.
- **Cover engagement:** During molding, the plastic cover flows around and between the projections. After solidification, the ribs mechanically interlock with the cover, resisting axial movement, rotation, and pullout.
- **Labyrinth seal:** The interfaces around the successive ribs create a long, tortuous path rather than a straight clearance from the battery interior to the exterior. Electrolyte or gas attempting to leak along the bushing-to-cover interface must repeatedly travel radially outward and inward around the projections. This greatly increases flow resistance and reduces capillary leakage.
- **Additional benefits:** The multiple ribs distribute mechanical loads and accommodate differences in thermal expansion between the conductive bushing and plastic cover. Sealing may be further improved by tight molding, surface treatments, or elastomeric sealants.

Thus, the same circumferential features both anchor the hollow terminal bushing in the cover and provide a multi-stage labyrinth barrier against electrolyte seepage.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style description of a rechargeable-battery bushing with a conical contacting section, an indented torque ring, and a concave lower inner-wall section.
counterfactuals.output:
## Rechargeable-Battery Bushing

A bushing (100) is provided for forming an electrically conductive terminal connection through a wall or cover (202) of a rechargeable-battery housing (200). The bushing (100) may be formed from lead, a lead alloy, copper, a copper alloy, or another electrically conductive material compatible with the electrochemical environment of the battery.

The bushing (100) extends along a longitudinal axis (A) between an upper end (102) and a lower end (104) and defines an axial passage (106) configured to receive a terminal post, pole, or other current-carrying member (204). The bushing includes a body portion (108), a conical contacting section (110), an indented torque ring (112), and a concave lower inner-wall section (114).

The conical contacting section (110) is disposed along at least part of an outer surface of the bushing (100). The conical contacting section tapers in the axial direction and is configured to engage a correspondingly shaped opening, seat, sealing member, or conductive interface associated with the battery cover (202). In one embodiment, the outer diameter of the conical contacting section decreases toward the lower end (104). The taper promotes axial centering of the bushing and provides an enlarged annular contact area when the bushing is pressed, molded, or otherwise secured within the battery cover. The conical contacting section may have a constant taper angle or may include multiple adjoining frustoconical regions having different taper angles.

The indented torque ring (112) is formed circumferentially around the outer surface of the bushing. The torque ring includes a plurality of circumferentially spaced indentations (116), recesses, grooves, flats, or serrations. Material of the battery cover, an overmolded polymer, or an intermediate sealing component may enter or engage the indentations (116), thereby resisting rotation of the bushing relative to the battery housing. The indentations may be formed by stamping, rolling, machining, casting, or molding. In certain embodiments, the torque ring is positioned axially adjacent to the conical contacting section (110), such that the conical contacting section resists axial displacement while the torque ring resists torsional displacement.

The axial passage (106) is bounded by an inner wall (118). A lower portion of the inner wall includes the concave lower inner-wall section (114). In longitudinal cross-section, the concave lower inner-wall section curves radially outward relative to an adjoining cylindrical or tapered section of the passage. The resulting enlarged or undercut region may receive displaced material during insertion, swaging, welding, or casting of the terminal post (204). The concave profile reduces abrupt internal transitions and distributes mechanical stresses over an extended axial region. It may also provide a retention pocket into which material of the terminal post flows, thereby improving resistance to axial separation and enhancing electrical contact between the post and the bushing.

An upper inner-wall section (120) may be substantially cylindrical, tapered, or stepped to guide insertion of the terminal post. A transition between the upper inner-wall section (120) and the concave lower inner-wall section (114) may be continuous and substantially free of sharp corners. The lower end (104) may further include an outwardly flared mouth (122) to facilitate insertion of the post or to accommodate deformation of the post during assembly.

During manufacture, the bushing (100) may be positioned in a mold and incorporated into the battery cover (202) by insert molding. Cover material engages the indentations (116) of the torque ring (112) and at least partially surrounds the conical contacting section (110). The terminal post (204) is subsequently inserted into the axial passage (106) and mechanically expanded, cast, soldered, brazed, or welded to the bushing. Expansion of the terminal post into the concave lower inner-wall section (114) establishes a mechanically interlocked and electrically conductive joint.

The combination of the conical contacting section, the indented torque ring, and the concave lower inner-wall section provides axial positioning, rotational restraint, improved sealing, and enhanced retention of the terminal post. These features may be formed integrally as a one-piece bushing or provided by joined components without departing from the disclosed configuration.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
